speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you point to exactly where it hurts, and did this start after a specific injury or fall?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old male. Mother has noticed a change in the child’s play patterns, specifically favoring his left leg while walking or running. The child complains of pain in his left knee, but denies any recent trauma or injury. He has no fever or other systemic symptoms. Nutrition and developmental milestones are appropriate for age.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the pain feel like it is located in his groin or thigh, or is it strictly in the knee? I am asking because hip pathology often presents as referred pain to the knee in children.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain localized to the left knee. I also have Limping favoring left leg, No fever, No systemic symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the pain radiate to the groin or thigh, and does he experience any limitation in internal rotation of the hip? I am trying to rule out slipped capital femoral epiphysis.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical or surgical history. Social history: The patient is in the second grade, lives with parents and one younger sibling. No exposure to tobacco or known toxins.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the pain worsen with activity or at night, and have you noticed any swelling or redness in the knee? I am trying to distinguish between transient synovitis and a more serious intra-articular pathology.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies recent illness, rash, weight loss, change in appetite or urinary symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: I need to assess his hip mobility directly; please attempt to internally rotate his left hip while it is extended and flexed to check for restriction. Also, does he experience any pain in the groin when walking or sitting?

speaker: Patient
text: Denies recent illness, rash, weight loss, change in appetite or urinary symptoms.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Flattening and fragmentation of the left femoral head consistent with Legg-Calvé-Perthes disease

speaker: Doctor
text: The X-ray confirms Legg-Calvé-Perthes disease with flattening and fragmentation of the left femoral head. DIAGNOSIS READY: Legg-Calvé-Perthes disease
